56a7704170: Echoing Iriving Park Lutheran Church's logo and the painting behind the altar, "Continuing the Journey" evokes the church's core values of welcoming all as they are in Christ's name on a shared journey of faith.
a86fe8f9b0: An abstract color theory mural with pixellated gradients of color mapped to a Roman block wall. The work is a contemporary example of abstract Impressionism and is inspired by the early video game and graphics development of Chicago's history (Midway Games et al). The work features smooth, pixellated color gradients which depict the flow of water and the reversal of the flow of the Chicago River, as well as a large, abstract "Irish Eye" to commemorate the Irish immigrants who died reversing the flow of the Chicago River in this historically Irish Bridgeport riverfront location. The mural also features ancient geometries found in Chicago's historic brick facades and in Mitla, Oaxaca, Mexico---the artist's nod to the Mexican heritage of the Pilsen neighborhood it faces.
89b29783f0: LAKE VIEW by Anthony Lewellen is an iconic 4,00 square-foot mural that celebrates Lakeview at an intersection that has historically served as the geographical center of the neighborhood. According to Lewellen, who grew up in Lakeview and has been a prominent figure in the Chicago arts community for decades, the artwork presents a visual metaphor that embodies the area's namesake and simultaneously plays with the notion of personification. "The central female figure, her hair flowing like waves, towers above the surrounding trees and buildings and in her reflected gaze, we see the horizon clear, blue, open and full of possibilities."
e5b9f274f0:
(Photo Credit: Sandra Steinbrecher) Brazilian artist, Eduardo Kobra specializes in “memory walls,” meaning that are specific to the community in which he is painting and evoke a certain nostalgia within the residents of that specific area. Chicago’s “memory wall” depicts legendary blues musician, Muddy Waters, was the perfect icon for this monumental wall.
The creation of this mural was a team effort and thanks go to several people, including Marc Realty, Beauty and Brawn Gallery & Think Space!
14e3094b0: Six Corners Association received a grant for the beautification of the Six Corners Business District. They passed that grant onto AAC with the goal of creating a mural for the 100' long brick wall on the west side of the 4935-37 Irving Park building. AAC contacted 5 local Artists and proposed a single mural on panels wherein each artist would showcase their trademark style in a somewhat loose narrative panorama. Penny Pinch, Shawnimals, Kathryn Eli, Carly Derec and Cyd Smillie each contributed to the mural.

2c94254130: Green Star Movement, with the help of approximately 500 volunteers, created this mosaic to celebrate the Woodlawn neighborhood and its culture. Elaborate portraits of notable figures, including Barack Obama, Michelle Obama, and singer Minnie Riperton are shaped out of tile. Photographs embedded in the material memorialize other former residents—including Emmett Till and Muhammad Ali. Further highlighting Woodlawn’s rich history, imagery from the front page of the Chicago Crusader, a newspaper headquartered in the neighborhood, is prominently displayed within the mosaic.
